title: Minimum Swaps to Sort by Digit Sum
summary: Given an array of distinct positive integers, determine the least number of swaps needed to arrange the array in ascending order based on the sum of the digits of each element.
statement: Given an array of distinct positive integers, determine the least number of swaps needed to arrange the array in ascending order based on the sum of the digits of each element. If two elements have the same digit sum, the smaller element should come first. A swap involves exchanging the values at two different positions in the array.
constraints: nums contains up to 100,000 distinct positive integers.
Order values by digit sum, breaking ties by the numerical value.
A swap may exchange any two positions; return the minimum count.
hints: Once the target order is fixed, current positions map to a permutation of target positions.
Sort by (digit sum,value), decompose the position mapping into cycles, and add cycle length minus one.
Build value-to-target-index, follow each unvisited cycle, and accumulate max(0,length-1).
A cycle of length L needs at least L-1 swaps and can always be corrected in exactly L-1 swaps; distinct values make the mapping unique.
editorial: A cycle of length L needs at least L-1 swaps and can always be corrected in exactly L-1 swaps; distinct values make the mapping unique.

tests.explanation: Digit sums are ten and one, so the two values need one swap.
Digit sums are already increasing from four through seven, so no swaps are needed.
